title: The seal gate passes silently when seals are deleted
evidence: COR-04.4's Debt: "removing a topic's lock entry and its pointer together passes `verify` whenever the topic cites no `sym:` id, because such a topic is then indistinguishable from one never sealed" (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/check.rs:391`-`392`). COR-05.1: a missing `seals.lock` is simply "no lock" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:441`-`445`). COR-06.2's Open: "Every topic of this repository's own corpus is such a topic" (path:line citers), and the migration step to `sym:` citations "is closed with the seal work" (`docs/DESIGN.md:26`-`30`).
failure: A contributor — or any automation with commit access — deletes `seals.lock` (or one topic's entry) and strips the `sealed:` pointer lines. `sealmap verify` exits 0 with zero findings on a path:line corpus; nothing in the tool records that a seal ever existed. CI reports the review record as intact when no topic is governed at all.
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt in COR-04.4, Open in COR-06.2) — but the aggregate consequence, that the entire corpus is ungovernable and the migration that would fix it is closed, is not marked.

title: Receipts and provenance attest consistency, not deployment; the binding is unkeyed
evidence: "Neither record asserts that a deployed consumer used those inputs" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:980`, `crates/sealmap-corpus/src/pack.rs:577`); "Adoption must cite a successful observation of the actual consumed version, rather than borrow success from another check"; "observations and authority are self-reported"; "A valid receipt is not a security certificate." The receipt binds findings by plain "SHA-256 binding" (COR-07.2); no key, signature or timestamp appears anywhere in the material — forgery of a self-consistent findings+receipt pair is possible by anyone with write access (inferred from the absence of any keyed material).
failure: A release process treats a green receipt as proof that the deployed consumer runs the reviewed fix. In fact the receipt establishes only internal consistency at check time; observations are self-reported strings; a rewritten findings file with a recomputed hash validates identically. The material contains no published-package, adoption or deployment evidence for any version, so this gap is undetectable from inside the workflow.
confidence: high for the attestation gap (stated); the forgery path is inferred
marked_by_authors: partially — the Open note covers self-reporting and the "not a sandbox" limit; the "neither asserts deployment" statement carries no marker.

title: The CI gate's own measurement shows it misses 24% of invalidating changes, and it is frozen
evidence: "per-symbol body hashes caught 0.76 of the changes that made a topic wrong, against 1.0 for per-file flags, while flagging only 1.19× fewer topics (`README.md:81`-`85`)"; "The seal surface is therefore experimental and frozen, not the recommended way to keep a corpus true (`docs/DESIGN.md:19`-`30`)." The `verify` gate still classifies per symbol (COR-04.5); only pack selection moved to files in 0.4.0.
failure: A team gates documentation freshness on `sealmap verify` in CI. Roughly one behaviour change in four that invalidates a cited topic passes the gate; the topic is silently wrong and trusted. "Frozen" means no fix is planned. Note the 0.76 figure is the project's own source-level experiment on blind-labelled commits, not a deployed measurement.
marked_by_authors: no marker; stated as prose caution in "For the business".

title: Diagrams systematically drop call-less control-flow arms; the corpus misrepresents the code it maps
evidence: "lowering drops any arm without a kept call (`crates/sealmap-extract/src/lower.rs:71`)", so the generated diagram of `classify` omits its unparsable arm and `sign` omits its success arm — "read from the generated corpus alone, both functions look as if they had no such path" (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/check.rs:146`, `crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/sign.rs:125`-`126`).
failure: Validation, early-return and fallback arms typically make no calls, so they vanish from every sequence diagram corpus-wide — including the seal checker itself, per the authors' own example. An agent consuming the corpus as facts models a function without its error paths and edits code accordingly; the incident lands in the consumer codebase. `_index.json` carries call lists, not control flow, so the loss is unrecoverable from the corpus.
confidence: high for the two named functions; the corpus-wide scope is inferred from the shared lowering site
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt) — but only for the two named functions; the general class is unmarked.

title: No defence against concurrent or hostile filesystem replacement during receipt validation
evidence: "The CLI is a local file checker, not a sandbox against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement"; artefact integrity is checked by reading bytes (`crates/sealmap/src/review_cli.rs:139`) with no freshness binding, lock, or re-check at consumption stated.
failure: Between validation and the downstream release decision, referenced artefacts are replaced on disk; the receipt remains "valid" as of check time and is cited in the audit. Alternatively any process with local write access rewrites findings, dispositions and artefacts before validation runs. Reachability requires local write access or an insider — severity is bounded by that.

title: A failed pack write leaves partial output in a newly created destination
evidence: "a failed write can still leave partial output in a newly created destination" — stated inside the output-path invariant (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:352` context). No cleanup or atomic rename is described; do not assume rollback from the failure.
failure: Disk fills mid-write; the command reports failure; `pack-01.txt` exists, truncated. A downstream job or reviewer reads it as the complete evidence pack; the review silently narrows to whatever was written before the failure.

title: Seals do not record the extraction options and naming that shaped their ids
evidence: "a seal must be checked with the flags it was signed with" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:73`-`74`) — yet the Debt says a seal does not record those flags, and the `Lock`/`TopicSeal` fields (COR-04.1, `lock.rs:57`) hold only opaque `reviewer`/`model` strings and fingerprints. The codebase name — which ids embed — defaults to the directory or repo names (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:393`).
failure: A checkout cloned under a different directory name, or CI running without `--tests` where the seal was signed with it, changes every id; sealed symbols classify as `Absent` and the gate fails with no code change. Diagnosing which flags a lock was signed with is impossible from the lock itself.

title: The topic set is internally inconsistent: stale pack semantics, missing commands, four different commit pins
evidence: `verified_commit` values across topics: `4ed7a51` (COR-01), `b9a6aeb` (COR-02/03/05), `eacc59e` (COR-04/06), `572e728` (COR-07) — no co-verification mechanism is shown. COR-05 states "pack itself is COR-06" with no supersession note, while COR-06 self-labels historical against COR-07. COR-07 changes documented behaviour: "Existing output paths are refused" and empty-selection-with-output "returns failure while preserving the previous file", versus COR-06.1's exit-0-writes-nothing and the `-o` stale-file Debt. COR-03.5's command inventory (`main.rs:45`-`71`, pinned `b9a6aeb`) lacks the `review` subcommands COR-07 adds (`review_cli.rs`).
failure: A pipeline built to COR-06 semantics (reusing `pack-01.txt` outputs, relying on exit 0 for an empty diff) breaks on 0.4.0: writes refused, exit codes changed. Engineers diagnosing an incident read COR-05/COR-03 instructions that no longer match the binary. Line citations across topics cannot all be valid at one checkout, and nothing tells the reader which topics are current.
marked_by_authors: no (COR-06's own "historical snapshot" header is the only marker; the stale pointers and mixed pins are not)

title: A CRLF checkout of the lock fails the whole gate as `LockFault`
evidence: `verify` demands canonical bytes and reports non-canonical as `LockFault`; only `Holds` passes (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/check.rs:104`-`105`). "`parse` alone normalises line endings, so a lock checked out with `\r\n` can be read and re-signed, while `verify` still reports it as not canonical (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/lock.rs:229`-`230`)."
failure: One Windows teammate or CI runner with translating git config commits or checks out the lock with CRLF; every `verify` elsewhere reports `LockFault` — a class that reads as tampering or hand-editing — and the gate is blocked team-wide until someone re-signs on an LF checkout or adds `.gitattributes`. Reaching CRLF bytes depends on checkout configuration (inferred).
confidence: high for the stated behaviour; medium overall, reachability inferred

title: Diagram truncation policy contradicts itself: some cuts are noted, three are not or are position-blind
evidence: The stated policy: "a diagram over its message or edge budget is cut, with a note saying how much was left out and where the full list is" (COR-02, business). Contradicted by: the trait map truncates to the first `max_edges` relations "in relation order rather than the heaviest, and writes no omitted count… a cut trait map is indistinguishable from a complete one" (`overview.rs:236`); unknown-receiver calls "under the default external policy such calls are dropped before they reach a diagram" (`naming.rs:47`-`49`); a sequence over `max_messages` drops calls "wherever they sit in the flow" with only a count (`sequence.rs:71`-`73`).
failure: An agent asks the trait map whether trait T is implemented anywhere; the edge was truncated and no note says so — the agent asserts "unimplemented" with the corpus's reliability behind it. Similarly, silently dropped unknown-receiver calls hide dependencies from traced flows.
marked_by_authors: yes (three Debts) — the contradiction with the stated business policy is unmarked.

title: Diff-based review selection and `stale --since` do not work for multi-repository codebases
evidence: "diff selection still requires a comparable single-repository baseline" (COR-07); `stale --since` outright "refuse[s] with `--repo`" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:461`-`462`); meanwhile multi-repo extraction and provenance are supported (`crates/sealmap/src/lib.rs:112`-`113`, `lib.rs:129`).
failure: An adopter with several repositories can build corpora and record provenance but cannot run `--diff` selection or `stale --since` across them. Reviews fall back to manual topic lists or per-repo runs against mismatched baselines, while "cross-repository uncertainty is not a reason to skip a topic" pushes the cost onto humans. Works for one repo, not for two.

title: Pack headers cannot distinguish different uncommitted working trees (`+dirty`)
evidence: Tension marker: "`+dirty` says that tracked files differ from `HEAD`, not how… Two packs of different uncommitted edits carry the same header. Their bodies differ, but the header alone cannot tell them apart" (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:769`-`770`). COR-07 does not restate the revision derivation, so whether this survives at `572e728` is not shown.
failure: Two reviewers pack two different uncommitted fixes from the same `HEAD`; both evidence files carry the identical revision line `HEAD+dirty`. Any record, audit or cache keyed on the pack header conflates two distinct evidence sets with no way to detect it from the header.
confidence: medium — stated at commit `eacc59e`; current-version behaviour not shown

title: Prose examples of `sym:` ids are indistinguishable from citations
evidence: Open: "an example id written in prose is indistinguishable from a citation (`crates/sealmap-corpus/src/seal/topic.rs:343`-`350`); the only escape is a fenced block, and nothing records whether topics that explain the grammar are meant to need one." `sign` refuses malformed citations (`sign.rs:122`); check keeps id-like spans with their error (`topic.rs:198`-`200`).
failure: The onboarding topic that documents the id grammar cites fabricated example ids. `seal sign` refuses them (if malformed) or seals non-existent symbols; `verify` flags `UnsealedCitation` indefinitely. Documentation of the system cannot pass the system's own gate without an undocumented fencing convention.

title: Reordering methods inside a sealed module fails the gate while every method holds
evidence: "a module's `body_hash` folds its members in source order (`crates/sealmap-rust/src/collect.rs:179`-`180`), so reordering methods inside a sealed module turns the module into `Behaviour` while every method holds (`crates/sealmap-corpus/tests/seal.rs:187`); a module is a poor thing to seal."
failure: A semantics-preserving reorder (IDE action, refactor) produces a `Behaviour` finding and a red gate. Repeated spurious resigns train the team to treat gate failures as noise, which is how F-01-style deletions stop being noticed.

title: `stale --since` and `pack --diff` need `tar` on PATH and leak temp directories when killed
evidence: "`--since` needs `tar` on the path as well as `git` (`crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:622`), and a process killed mid-run leaves its `sealmap-since-*` directory in the system temp directory, since only a normal drop removes it (`main.rs:644`-`646`)."
failure: A minimal CI image without `tar` makes both diff workflows exit 2 ("could not run"). CI runners killed on timeout accumulate `sealmap-since-*` trees in `/tmp` on shared long-lived hosts until the disk fills.

title: The verification gate is blind to changes outside cited symbols; a topic that had become false passed as "holds"
evidence: The authors' own measurement — per-symbol body hashes caught 0.76 of the changes that made a topic wrong, against 1.0 for per-file flags (`README.md:81`-`85`); the design states the seal surface is "experimental and frozen, not the recommended way to keep a corpus true" (`docs/DESIGN.md:19`-`30`); `pack --diff`'s per-symbol rule "loses real changes" and is "a convenience, not an answer" (`README.md:41`-`46`, `README.md:291`); the 0.4.0 change exists precisely because "its measured recall was inadequate as a skipping gate" (COR-07, developers section, `pack/selection.rs:25`).
failure: A pipeline gates a client-facing release on `sealmap verify` exiting 0. An engineer lands a change that alters behaviour a topic describes — in code the topic never cites, or by moving code so hashes match (COR-06.4: "A move is not a change", `pack.rs:383`-`387`). `verify` compares only each sealed symbol's `sig` and `body` hashes (`check.rs:147`, `check.rs:150`) and the prose hash (`check.rs:271`-`275`); nothing binds uncited files. Every finding is `Holds`, only `Holds` passes (`check.rs:45`-`46`), the gate is green, and a false claim about how data is handled ships to the client. For topics that never migrated to `sym:` citations the gate is weaker still: they are "coverage, not failures" (`docs/DESIGN.md:161`-`163`).
confidence: medium — the blind spot is stated by the material; that the operator gated a release on it is inferred.

title: Receipts and routing declarations validate recorded shape, not what any runtime actually executed or consumed
evidence: "Adoption must cite a successful observation of the actual consumed version, rather than borrow success from another check" — a rule about recorded strings, not runtime truth (COR-07, developers); "These APIs neither invoke models nor attest which model a service actually runs" (same section); "A valid receipt is not a security certificate" and "two reviewers agreeing does not verify a finding" (COR-07, business); "The CLI is a local file checker, not a sandbox against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement" (COR-07.2, Open).
failure: The operator declares routes and tiers mapping client activities to named providers (`route.rs:283`, `tiers.rs:141`) and records repair evidence in receipts. A provider serves a different model or version than declared, or a stale gateway config persists after a repair. `pack_provenance` records repository baselines and build-context hashes (`main.rs:980`) and the pack header binds extraction input bytes (`pack.rs:577`), but "Neither record asserts that a deployed consumer used those inputs." `review::validate` and the CLI check binding, dispositions and referenced artefact bytes locally (`review.rs:339`, `review_cli.rs:139`); the "observed success" entries are self-reported (COR-07.2, Open). Everything validates green while client data was processed by an unattested model or tier — a custody/security failure with no signal from the tool.
confidence: medium — the attestation gap is stated; the operator's reliance on receipts/declarations as runtime proof is inferred.

title: Review evidence was silently incomplete: truncation without a marker, and the corpus's own diagrams of the seal code omit arms
evidence: The three author-flagged silent-omission debts above; the corpus README warns diagrams are summaries but the trait-map cut carries no marker at all (`overview.rs:236`); dropped sequence calls are "recoverable from `_index.json`, not from the diagram" (`sequence.rs:71`-`73`), so a diagram-only reader has no way to know what is missing in the trait-map case.
failure: A reviewer or agent consults the generated corpus — which the material says is "what an agent reads when it needs the facts about a file without opening the code" (COR-01, business). The trait map it reads was cut at `max_edges` with no omitted count, so it "is indistinguishable from a complete one" (`overview.rs:236`); or a sequence it reads was cut at the 80-message default and "drops every later call from the diagram, wherever it sits in the flow" (`sequence.rs:71`-`73`, `lib.rs:162`) — the dropped tail holding the write, delete or external call that mattered. The agent or reviewer approves a change on the incomplete picture; the production defect follows. The same class corrupts the corpus's self-description: the generated diagrams of `classify` and `sign` omit arms, so "read from the generated corpus alone, both functions look as if they had no such path" (`lower.rs:71`, `check.rs:146`, `sign.rs:125`-`126`).
confidence: medium — the omissions are stated; the path from omission to this incident is inferred.

title: A seal can be silently removed from a topic that cites no `sym:` ids
evidence: Removing a topic's lock entry and its pointer together passes `verify` whenever the topic cites no `sym:` id, "because such a topic is then indistinguishable from one never sealed... nothing remembers that a topic was once sealed" (`check.rs:391`-`392`).
failure: A reviewed topic's review record is deleted together with its pointer; the gate stays green and the topic drops to coverage-only. Durable effect: the lock no longer contains the entry, so no later check can reconstruct that a seal existed.

title: An empty diff leaves the previous pack on disk at the output path
evidence: With nothing changed, `pack --diff` exits 0 and writes nothing; with `-o FILE` "a pack from an earlier run is left in place, where a caller may read it as current" (`main.rs:712`-`714`). The 0.4.0 behaviour returns failure for an empty selection with an output path "while preserving the previous file", and "existing output paths are refused" (`main.rs:352`), so the stale file is never overwritten by a retry — only manual deletion replaces it.
failure: A consumer that reads the path without checking the exit code reviews yesterday's evidence as current. Durable effect: the stale pack persists on disk; retry cannot repair it.
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt in COR-06.1; the 0.4.0 preserve-and-refuse behaviour is stated as an invariant, unflagged)

title: A failed write can leave partial output in a newly created destination
evidence: "A failed write can still leave partial output in a newly created destination" (`main.rs:352` context, COR-07.1 invariant text).
failure: A consumer reads a truncated pack from the new path; a retry refuses the now-existing path, so retry does not repair — the partial file is durable until deleted by hand.

title: `stale` always exits 0
evidence: `stale` returns 0 even when it lists changed sealed symbols (`main.rs:599`, `docs/DESIGN.md:157`); the design intends it as a report, not a gate.
failure: Any script branching on exit code treats "changes found" as pass; drift reports are produced but never acted on.
confidence: high on the behaviour; the failure scenario is inferred

title: Seals do not record the extraction options or codebase name that shaped their ids
evidence: A lock signed with `--tests` and checked without it reports test symbols as absent; "only the flag's doc comment says so" (`main.rs:73`-`74`). The codebase name defaults to `--name`, the directory, or the repo names (`main.rs:393`), and "checking a seal with different settings from the ones it was signed with makes sealed functions look absent" (COR-05, business).
failure: A directory rename or flag change produces mass `Absent` findings; the gate blocks releases until seals are deleted or re-signed — either availability loss or silent loss of review history.

title: A prose example that looks like an id is a citation
evidence: "An example id written in prose is indistinguishable from a citation" (`topic.rs:343`-`350`); the only escape is a fenced block, and a span that parses is kept as a citation (`topic.rs:198`-`200`).
failure: A topic explaining the grammar either fails sign/verify on a malformed example (loud), or a well-formed example resolves and is sealed and verified — binding the review record to symbols the prose never meant to cite.
confidence: high on indistinguishability; the wrong-binding scenario is inferred

title: Module body hashes are order-sensitive
evidence: A module's `body_hash` folds members in source order (`collect.rs:179`-`180`); reordering methods flips the module to `Behaviour` while every method holds (`tests/seal.rs:187`); "a module is a poor thing to seal."
failure: Routine reordering produces persistent `Behaviour` noise, training reviewers to disregard the class that also carries real changes.

title: Every release rewrites `_index.json` and fails `generate --check`
evidence: The index records the generator as `sealmap-corpus` plus crate version (`index.rs:104`), so "a version bump with no other change rewrites `_index.json`, and a kept copy reports drift... on every release."
failure: Operators who keep a copy see drift on every release; the check is removed or ignored, and a later real drift is missed.

title: The `+dirty` revision marker cannot distinguish different uncommitted states
evidence: `+dirty` says tracked files differ from `HEAD`, "not how"; "Two packs of different uncommitted edits carry the same header" (`main.rs:769`-`770`).
failure: Two packs from materially different dirty states share a provenance header; an auditor cannot tell which state a pack was taken from. COR-07 binds extraction input bytes and build-context hashes (`pack.rs:577`, `main.rs:980`), which binds the body, but whether the 0.4.0 revision line retains the coarse dirty flag is not stated.
confidence: high for the historical header; persistence in 0.4.0 not judgeable

title: `--since` needs `tar` on the PATH and leaks the exported revision on abnormal exit
evidence: `--since` pipes a git archive through `tar -x` (`main.rs:622`); only a normal drop removes the temp directory, so "a process killed mid-run leaves its `sealmap-since-*` directory in the system temp directory" (`main.rs:644`-`646`).
failure: In restricted CI, a missing `tar` makes `--since` and `pack --diff` unavailable (loud). On a shared machine, a killed run leaves a full export of the repository's source tree world-readable in system temp until cleaned — an unattended source disclosure.
confidence: high on both stated behaviours; the disclosure consequence is inferred

title: A pack of `path:line` topics carries no code evidence at all
evidence: "A topic that cites `path:line` rather than `sym:` ids packs as its text alone" (`docs/DESIGN.md:232`-`233`), and "every topic of this repository's own corpus is such a topic" (`docs/DESIGN.md:26`-`30`).
failure: A reviewer receives the claims with no slices and no source windows; the review degenerates to trusting the topic text and can approve a false claim.
confidence: high on the behaviour; the approval failure is inferred

title: A move is not a change
evidence: `SymbolState` compares hashes and "never its place" (`pack.rs:383`-`387`); "A move is not a change."
failure: A function relocated into a different module or visibility context keeps its body hash; `--diff` does not select topics citing it, and its old citation resolving absent is surfaced only if someone packs or resolves that topic — which selection just decided not to do.
confidence: high on the behaviour; the failure chain is inferred

title: Calls on unknown receivers collapse into one `?` lane and are dropped under the default external policy
evidence: Every call on a receiver of unknown type shares one `?` lane (`naming.rs:47`-`49`), and "under the default external policy such calls are dropped before they reach a diagram" (COR-02.2 Debt; default is `CrateRoot`, `naming.rs:59`-`64`).
failure: A call through a dynamic receiver — e.g., a trait object or FFI handle performing the actual write — never appears in any sequence; an agent reading the diagram concludes the function makes no such call.

title: Artefact checks are not a sandbox against concurrent file replacement
evidence: "The CLI is a local file checker, not a sandbox against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement" (COR-07.2, Open); the CLI checks referenced artefact bytes (`review_cli.rs:139`).
failure: An artefact is swapped between the byte check and its later use; validation reports intact bytes the process never actually consumed — a check-to-use gap with no boundary that would falsify it later.
confidence: high that no sandboxing exists; the exploit scenario is inferred

title: Diff selection requires a single-repository baseline; multi-repository reviews cannot use it
evidence: "Multi-repository provenance is supported; diff selection still requires a comparable single-repository baseline. Cross-repository uncertainty is not a reason to skip a topic" (COR-07, developers). What happens on a multi-repo diff attempt — refusal, error, or empty selection — is not stated; only the empty-selection-with-output-path failure is specified (`main.rs:352` context).
failure: A multi-repo operator's diff step either fails or silently reviews nothing; the "not a reason to skip" guidance is prose, not enforced selection behaviour.
confidence: medium — the constraint is stated, the outcome on violation is not
